posts.name: Gregory Lee Bartholomew
posts.cooked:
Beka Tabidze:
  1. I want to add specific settings to panel or to apps menu, specifically printing options for specific printer. Would this be possible? Image

Maybe. Many (but not all) buttons will cause a command to be run. If you can identify the command line that is triggered when clicking that button, then you might be able to put that command on the Exec=... line of a .desktop file and save it under ~/.local/share/applications.[1]

Alternatively, you might be able to write a .desktop file or two that directly sets the option(s) you are interested in. Does the option you want to change appear in the output of the lpoptions command?

  1. See /usr/share/applications for example .desktop files. ↩︎

posts.name: Sakiko Togawa
posts.cooked:
For the 2nd issue about creating a Windows installation media: I recently created a Windows 10 USB installation media using WoeUSB (the CLI version of WoeUSB-NG). However, WoeUSB is currently an orphaned package and only available on Fedora 41 (Workstation w/ GNOME DE). I first installed Fedora 41, used it to create the Windows 10 installation media with WoeUSB, and then replaced Fedora 41 with Windows 10.

Install the necessary packages:

sudo dnf install woeusb grub2-tools

Create the installation media:

sudo woeusb --target-filesystem NTFS --device /path/to/windows.iso /dev/sdX

Replace /path/to/windows.iso with the actual path to Windows ISO file, and /dev/sdX with the path to the USB device.

If WoeUSB complains target device is busy, unmount the USB device. Identify the device using lsblk, and then unmount them with:

sudo umount /dev/sdX*

posts.name: Gregory Lee Bartholomew
posts.cooked:
Beka Tabidze:

One of the options I want doesn’t seems to be available in lpoptions.
How do I identify what command is being run?

It appears to be running gnome-control-center printers, and beyond that, it is communicating with the CUPS backend.[1]

$ lsof -p <pid-of-running-gnome-control-center-command>
...
gnome-con 5414 gregory  mem       REG               0,34    145184  577760 /usr/lib64/gtk-4.0/4.0.0/printbackends/libprintbackend-cups.so
...

I think lpoptions should be the right command line interface for CUPS. What setting is missing? They should all be there, except for a few higher-level settings like who can access the printer and printer quotas. The remaining settings would be configured via lpadmin.

  1. GitLab

    gtk/print/backends/gtkprintbackendcups.c · main · GNOME / gtk · GitLab

    GTK is a multi-platform toolkit for creating graphical user interfaces.

    ↩︎

posts.name: Gregory Lee Bartholomew
posts.cooked:
Try lpoptions -o orientation-requested=N where N is a number from 3-6.

Excerpted from cups.org – options – Setting the Orientation:

  • -o orientation-requested=3 - portrait orientation (no rotation)
  • -o orientation-requested=4 - landscape orientation (90 degrees)
  • -o orientation-requested=5 - reverse landscape or seascape orientation (270 degrees)
  • -o orientation-requested=6 - reverse portrait or upside-down orientation (180 degrees)

posts.name: Przemek Klosowski
posts.cooked:
Don’t give up, you can do it!
You just have to figure out how the pieces work together. This is generally true in Linux, so the sooner you learn it the happier you will be using it in the long term.
Gregory suggested that a script (which is just a disk file with shell commands that is marked as executable, e.g. by ‘‘chmod +x yourScriptFilename’’ ) containing the command
‘’‘lpoptions -o orientation-requested=4’‘’
will switch to landscape mode. You can then create a file in ~/.local/share/applications/landscape.desktop containing
[Desktop Entry]
Type=Application
Name=switch printer to portrait
Exec=yourScriptFilename

This may be a little tedious, but once you understand how it works, you can do other more complex things, perhaps using other, fancier tools.

posts.name: Espionage724
posts.cooked:
Beka Tabidze:

Tool for installing Windows on Flash drive other than Ventoy? I tried Woeusb-ng and it doesn’ work, after some googling I think it doesn’t work specifically on gnome. Any other options?

wget -O '/tmp/woeusb.bash' 'https://github.com/WoeUSB/WoeUSB/releases/download/v5.2.4/woeusb-5.2.4.bash' && chmod +x '/tmp/woeusb.bash'

sudo dnf install 'wimlib-utils' -y && sync

sudo '/tmp/woeusb.bash' --device ~/'Downloads/en-us_windows_10_iot_enterprise_ltsc_2021_x64_dvd_257ad90f.iso' '/dev/sda' && sync

The wimlib package is a little different depending on distro (Ubuntu is wimtools), but I used those commands for a couple years like that.
